claim: The hippocampus is grossly comprised of five excitatory cell populations: granule and mossy cells of the dentate gyrus (DG), and pyramidal cells of CA3, CA2, and CA1.
source: The hippocampus is grossly comprised of five excitatory cell populations; namely, granule and mossy cells of the dentate gyrus (DG), and pyramidal cells of CA3, CA2, and CA1.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the manuscript describing the composition of the hippocampus.

claim: Replicate datasets corresponding to the same class-region pair were well correlated with each other (r = 0.98 ± 0.02, mean ± SD, Pearson's correlation coefficient).
source: Replicate datasets, corresponding to the same class-region pair, were well correlated with each other (r = 0.98 ± 0.02, mean ± SD, Pearson's correlation coefficient; Figure 1—figure supplement 2a,b)
evidence: The manuscript reports quantitative correlation coefficients from the RNA-seq data analysis.

claim: Each replicate was devoid of marker gene cohorts associated with interneurons and non-neuronal cells.
source: each replicate was devoid of marker gene cohorts associated with interneurons and non-neuronal cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2d).
evidence: The manuscript reports analysis of marker genes showing absence of contaminating cell types.

claim: The initial bifurcation in hierarchical clustering corresponded to a divide between granule cells and non-granule cells.
source: Using hierarchical clustering (see Materials and methods; Figure 2a) we found the initial bifurcation corresponded to a divide between granule cells and non-granule cells, consistent with previous microarray (Greene et al., 2009) and ISH work (Thompson et al., 2008).
evidence: The manuscript reports results from hierarchical clustering analysis and cites previous work supporting this finding.

claim: The second broad division of the dendrogram partitioned mossy cells from pyramidal cells.
source: The second broad division of the dendrogram partitioned mossy cells from pyramidal cells
evidence: The manuscript describes the hierarchical clustering results.

claim: The final bifurcation in each limb corresponded to dorsal-ventral differences in each cell class.
source: the final bifurcation in each limb corresponded to dorsal-ventral differences in each cell class
evidence: The manuscript describes the hierarchical clustering results.

claim: RNA-seq marker genes gave good agreement with ABA histological data, correctly predicting the enriched populations in ~81% of cases (124/153 genes where coronal ISH images were available).
source: Importantly, these RNA-seq hits gave good agreement with ABA histological data, correctly predicting the enriched populations in ~81% of cases (124/153 genes where coronal ISH images were available, Figure 2b, Supplementary file 1; see Materials and methods).
evidence: The manuscript reports quantitative validation of RNA-seq results against ISH data.

claim: 41 genes were identified with >3-fold enrichment in CA2 relative to all other populations.
source: This search identified 41 genes with >3-fold enrichment in CA2 relative to all other populations, using relatively conservative search parameters (Figure 3a,b; see Materials and methods).
evidence: The manuscript reports the number of CA2-enriched genes identified from RNA-seq analysis.

claim: 66% (n=27/41) of CA2-enriched genes discovered were novel hits not previously identified.
source: Notably, although some of our retrieved genes were previously identified as enriched in CA2 (Figure 3a), the majority of discovered genes were novel hits (66%, n=27/41; Figure 3b).
evidence: The manuscript reports quantitative comparison of newly identified genes versus previously known genes.

claim: CA3, CA2, and CA1 each had a similar number of enriched genes when restricting comparisons to solely these three cell populations in the dorsal hippocampus.
source: Analyzing gene expression in dorsal CA3, CA2, and CA1, we found each cell population had a similar number of enriched genes (Figure 3c).
evidence: The manuscript reports results from differential expression analysis.

claim: CA3, CA2, and CA1 regions were approximately equidistant in multidimensional scaling analysis.
source: Complementing this, applying multidimensional scaling to visualize the distances between CA3, CA2, and CA1 (see Materials and methods), we found that the three regions were approximately equidistant (Figure 3d).
evidence: The manuscript reports results from multidimensional scaling analysis.

claim: CA2 is largely its own distinct region, rather than being a weighted combination of CA3 and CA1 features.
source: These results illustrated that CA2 is largely its own distinct region, rather than being a weighted combination of CA3 and CA1 features; i.e., the physical intermediacy of CA2 did not correlate with transcriptional intermediacy.
evidence: The manuscript interprets the multidimensional scaling and enrichment analysis results.

claim: Previous work has found one gene enriched in mossy cells (Calb2).
source: Previous work has found one gene enriched in mossy cells (Calb2) (Fujise et al., 1998), which was recapitulated by our analysis (Figure 4a)
evidence: The manuscript cites previous literature and confirms the finding with their data.

claim: 59 mossy cell-enriched genes in the hippocampus were identified.
source: in addition we identified 59 mossy cell-enriched genes in the hippocampus (Figure 4b).
evidence: The manuscript reports the number of mossy cell-enriched genes identified from RNA-seq analysis.

claim: 95% (n=36/38) of mossy cell-enriched genes from RNA-seq showed agreement with expression in hilar cells in the ABA where coronal images were available.
source: Cross-validating these genes in the ABA, we found excellent agreement between mossy cell-enriched genes from RNA-seq and expression in the hilar cells (95%; n=36/38 agreement where coronal images available, Supplementary file 2; see Materials and methods).
evidence: The manuscript reports quantitative validation of RNA-seq results against ISH data.

claim: Mossy cells are a transcriptionally heterogeneous population of cells.
source: In addition to this differential labeling across the hippocampus, differences were also seen in the labeling density at corresponding enriched regions (e.g., cf. Nmb with Thbs2 dorsally and Calb2 with Csf2rb2 ventrally), suggesting that mossy cells are a transcriptionally heterogeneous population of cells.
evidence: The manuscript infers heterogeneity from observed differential gene expression patterns.

claim: The dorsal marker gene Lct and the ventral marker Trhr may correspond to tripartite molecular divisions of the dentate gyrus.
source: Previous work (Fanselow and Dong, 2010) has suggested that domains specified by the dorsal marker gene Lct and the ventral marker Trhr may correspond to tripartite molecular divisions of the dentate gyrus (Figure 5a): here, Lct and Trhr expression respectively represent the dorsal and ventral divisions, whereas the intermediate domain is characterized by weak expression of both genes.
evidence: The manuscript cites previous work proposing this organization.

claim: RNA-seq work recapitulated both Lct and Trhr as marker genes for dorsal and ventral granule cells.
source: Importantly, our RNA-seq work recapitulated both of these marker genes, suggesting that our data could be used to quantitatively explore the degree and patterns of granule cell heterogeneity.
evidence: The manuscript reports that their data confirmed previously identified markers.

claim: Hundreds of genes were differentially expressed between dorsal and ventral poles of dentate gyrus granule cells.
source: Notably, hundreds of genes were differentially expressed between these two poles (Figure 5b), and corresponded to large fold changes (Figure 5c).
evidence: The manuscript reports results from differential expression analysis.

claim: 58% (n=33/57) of differentially expressed granule cell genes showed agreement with ISH where coronal images were available.
source: Many of these genes were involved in neuronally relevant functions and were cross-validated by ISH (58%, n=33/57 agreement where coronal images available, Figure 5—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 3; see Materials and methods).
evidence: The manuscript reports quantitative validation of RNA-seq results against ISH data.

claim: The genetic domain specified by Lct was recapitulated by multiple dorsal marker genes.
source: The genetic domain specified by Lct was recapitulated by multiple dorsal marker genes (Figure 5—figure supplement 1b), including Gsg1l, Spata13, and Stra6 (Figure 5d).
evidence: The manuscript reports ISH validation showing consistent spatial patterns.

claim: Little agreement was seen between ventral marker genes in terms of spatial domains.
source: Conversely, little agreement was seen between ventral marker genes: the domain specified by Trhr was found to differ from the patterns observed for other markers (e.g., Cpne7, Grp, and Nr2f2; Figure 5e, Figure 5—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: The manuscript reports ISH validation showing inconsistent spatial patterns.

claim: The genetic boundary defined by Lct may correspond to a transcriptionally well-defined subpopulation, but an equally well-defined ventral subpopulation does not appear to be present.
source: These findings indicate that the genetic boundary defined by Lct may correspond to a transcriptionally well-defined subpopulation, but an equally well-defined ventral subpopulation does not appear to be present.
evidence: The manuscript infers this conclusion from the differential spatial patterns observed.

claim: All novel granule cell marker genes validated by ISH appeared to be expressed in gradients across the long axis.
source: Despite this, all novel marker genes validated by ISH appeared to be expressed in gradients across the long axis (Figure 5—figure supplement 1b,c; we did not find genes that were selectively expressed in either the upper or lower blades of DG granule cells), suggesting that granule cell transcriptional identity exists in a continuous spectrum in this axis.
evidence: The manuscript reports ISH observations and infers continuous variation.

claim: Lct is expressed in dorsal CA1 and Trhr is expressed in ventral CA3.
source: The granule cell marker genes Lct and Trhr were previously shown to be enriched in other class-region populations; namely, Lct is expressed in dorsal CA1 and Trhr is expressed in ventral CA3 (Cembrowski et al., 2016; Dong et al., 2009; Thompson et al., 2008) (see also Figure 5a).
evidence: The manuscript cites previous work showing expression patterns.

claim: Cadm2 and Mgll were found to be >2 fold dorsally enriched in every dorsal-ventral comparison.
source: e.g., the genes Cadm2 and Mgll were found to be >2 fold dorsally enriched in every dorsal-ventral comparison, whereas Resp18 and Efnb2 were found to be ventrally enriched (Figure 6b; corroborated by ABA, Figure 6d).
evidence: The manuscript reports results from differential expression analysis across multiple cell classes.

claim: Resp18 and Efnb2 were found to be ventrally enriched in every dorsal-ventral comparison.
source: e.g., the genes Cadm2 and Mgll were found to be >2 fold dorsally enriched in every dorsal-ventral comparison, whereas Resp18 and Efnb2 were found to be ventrally enriched (Figure 6b; corroborated by ABA, Figure 6d).
evidence: The manuscript reports results from differential expression analysis across multiple cell classes.

claim: In almost every possible comparison (n=5/6 pairwise enrichment combinations and 2/2 triplicate enrichment combinations), the number of enriched genes that were shared across cell classes in a region-specific manner were significantly greater than that expected by chance.
source: Interestingly, in almost every possible comparison (n=5/6 pairwise enrichment combinations and 2/2 triplicate enrichment combinations), the number of enriched genes that were shared across cell classes in a region-specific manner were significantly greater than that expected by chance.
evidence: The manuscript reports statistical comparison to a null model.

claim: 37 genes were found enriched in a region-specific manner across all principal cells of the trisynaptic loop.
source: We examined the ontologies associated with the 37 genes that were enriched across all dorsal-ventral comparisons (i.e., the n=12 dorsally and 25 ventrally enriched genes from the triplicate comparisons of Figure 6c).
evidence: The manuscript reports the number of genes identified from differential expression analysis.

claim: Many genes that emerged as being region- but not class-enriched corresponded to cellular adhesion and axon guidance.
source: Although the enriched genes spanned a variety of ontologies, many genes that emerged as being region- but not class-enriched corresponded to cellular adhesion and axon guidance; for example, the cellular adhesion molecules Cadm1, Cadm2, the ephrins/receptors Epha5, Epha7, Efnb2, as well as Dagla, Odz4, Timp2 and Negr1 (Figure 6e).
evidence: The manuscript reports ontology analysis results.

claim: 43% (n=16/37) of genes identified as regionally enriched in all principal cells of the trisynaptic loop were identified as differentially expressed in the dorsal-ventral axis of MEC with an identical directionality.
source: Strikingly, of the 37 genes identified as regionally enriched in all principal cells of the trisynaptic loop, 43% (n=16/37) were identified as differentially expressed in the dorsal-ventral axis of MEC with an identical directionality (Figure 6e, orange text).
evidence: The manuscript reports comparison with published MEC RNA-seq data.

claim: WGCNA identified eight gene modules that were enriched in various subpopulations of hippocampal excitatory neurons.
source: We used the top 1000 most variable genes from the full hippocampal dataset, and using WGCNA, identified eight gene modules that were enriched in various subpopulations of hippocampal excitatory neurons (Figure 7a,b; see Materials and methods).
evidence: The manuscript reports results from WGCNA analysis.

claim: The KEGG annotation 'Long Term Potentiation' was enriched for distinct modules associated with DG granule cells, CA1 pyramidal cells, and CA2/3 pyramidal cells.
source: For example, the KEGG annotation 'Long Term Potentiation' was enriched for distinct modules associated with DG granule cells, CA1 pyramidal cells, and CA2/3 pyramidal cells (Figure 7c), illustrating that specific genes that underlie LTP vary between cell classes despite all cell classes expressing genes related to LTP.
evidence: The manuscript reports results from ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: Both mossy cells and dorsal dentate gyrus granule cells were enriched for genes associated with Parkinson's disease.
source: Similarly, this approach also enabled us to identify specific modules with disease annotations; for example, both mossy cells and dorsal dentate gyrus granule cells were enriched for genes associated with disease terms (e.g., Parkinson's; Figure 7d).
evidence: The manuscript reports results from disease ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: On average, 112 ± 6 cells per biological replicate were purified by manual selection.
source: The sorted sample underwent library preparation and sequencing, the resulting raw RNA-seq reads were aligned, and expression was quantified and analyzed across samples (see Materials and methods).
evidence: The manuscript reports the number of cells used in the experimental protocol.

claim: Three biological replicates were ascertained for each dataset.
source: To assess reproducibility, three biological replicates were ascertained for each dataset.
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental design.

claim: 77.5 ± 1.0% (29.6 ± 2.0 million per replicate) of all reads aligned at least once to either the annotated transcriptome or genome.
source: With these settings, 77.5 ± 1.0% (29.6 ± 2.0 million per replicate, n = 24) of all reads aligned at least once to either the annotated transcriptome or genome.
evidence: The manuscript reports alignment statistics from RNA-seq data processing.

claim: FPKM values for ERCC spike-in controls were highly reproducible across replicates (r = 0.94 ± 0.01, n = 24 replicates).
source: When considering spike-in controls, FPKM values were found to be highly reproducible across replicates (r = 0.94 ± 0.01, n = 24 replicates, Pearson correlation coefficient).
evidence: The manuscript reports correlation analysis of spike-in controls.

claim: A conventional threshold of FDR <0.05 was used for differential expression.
source: General analysis conventions were as follows: a conventional threshold of FDR <0.05 was used for differential expression, allowing both under- and overexpressed genes to be identified (i.e., two-sided)
evidence: The manuscript describes the statistical threshold used in analysis.

claim: Gene expression was required to obey FPKM>10 in at least one population to be included in differential expression or enriched population analyses.
source: gene expression was required to obey FPKM>10 in at least one population to be included in differential expression or enriched population analyses.

source: Raw and processed RNA-seq datasets were deposited in the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO), accession number GSE74985

claim: The transcriptional distance between dorsal and ventral granule cells is similar to that between different populations of cells.
source: Indeed, the transcriptional distance between dorsal and ventral granule cells is similar to that between different populations of cells (Figure 2a), a finding similar to that found between CA3 and CA1 pyramidal cells (Figure 2a) (Cembrowski et al., 2016).
evidence: The manuscript interprets hierarchical clustering results and cites previous work.

claim: Many region-enriched genes are involved in cell adhesion and axon guidance.
source: The fact that many of these genes are involved in cell adhesion and axon guidance, in conjunction with the observation that they are enriched along the dorsal-ventral axis in multiple areas of the brain, suggests that they may generally be used for maintaining polarity in the mature brain.
evidence: The manuscript infers functional implications from gene ontology analysis.

claim: Region-enriched genes may be used for maintaining polarity in the mature brain.
source: The fact that many of these genes are involved in cell adhesion and axon guidance, in conjunction with the observation that they are enriched along the dorsal-ventral axis in multiple areas of the brain, suggests that they may generally be used for maintaining polarity in the mature brain.

claim: During development, gradients of gene expression are used for proper patterning of neural circuits.
source: During development, gradients of gene expression are used for proper patterning of neural circuits (Sansom and Livesey, 2009)

claim: Region-enriched genes may reflect the mature counterpart that actively maintains spatial identity.
source: in a similar fashion, these genes may reflect the mature counterpart that actively maintains spatial identity.

claim: CA3 pyramidal cells have been shown to conform to discrete subpopulations.
source: for example, CA3 pyramidal cells have been shown to conform to discrete subpopulations (Thompson et al., 2008)

source: whereas CA1 pyramidal cells (Cembrowski et al., 2016), DG mossy cells (Figure 4), and DG granule cells (Figure 5) do not exhibit clear subdomain organization.
evidence: The manuscript cites previous work and their own data showing lack of discrete subdomains.

claim: The results likely underestimate the total amount of variability in principal cells of the hippocampus.
source: It is important to emphasize that our results, although illustrating a high degree of transcriptional heterogeneity in principal cells of the hippocampus, likely underestimate the total amount of variability for several reasons.
evidence: The manuscript acknowledges limitations of their approach.

claim: Comparing the dorsal and ventral poles may miss differences present along other dimensions, as well as differences present at spatially intermediate locations.
source: First, comparing the dorsal and ventral poles may miss differences present along other dimensions, as well as differences present at spatially intermediate locations.

claim: The population-level approach may miss heterogeneity that is present at a subpopulation or single-cell level.
source: Second, our population-level approach may miss heterogeneity that is present at a subpopulation or single-cell level, including transcriptional signatures associated with specialized but sparse excitatory cell classes (e.g., radiatum giant cells (Gulyas et al., 1998), semilunar granule cells (Williams et al., 2007), and CA3 granule cells (Szabadics et al., 2010)).

source: All data presented here are accessible on the Hipposeq website (http://hipposeq.janelia.org), an interactive database that allows user-friendly analysis and visualization of gene expression data for individual genes, cohorts of genes, and entire transcriptomes.

claim: RNA-seq offers advantages that circumvent traditional issues associated with ISH, including providing class-specific data with a large dynamic range.
source: Our RNA-seq approach offers advantages that circumvent traditional issues associated with ISH; namely, providing class-specific data with a large dynamic range, helping to circumvent confounds associated with image-based analyses of gene expression that can be limited by changes in cell density and/or labeling across sections.

claim: RNA-seq has limitations relative to ISH, including an inherent lack of spatial information.
